checks.finding: requirements.md's REQ-006 Goals text ("specify a single classification — for every check REQ-001 through REQ-005 name — of whether it is fully automatable today...") and AC-025 ("A single classification table (design.md) lists every check REQ-001 through REQ-005 name and marks each one automated, automated-pending-confirmation..., or manual-required... — exhaustive over every check this package names, never partial") explicitly scope the normative Automated/Manual Classification Table to REQ-001 through REQ-005's checks only (i.e. AC-001–AC-024/AC-028's REQ-003 lineage), excluding REQ-006's and REQ-007's own checks (AC-025–AC-027, AC-029–AC-030). But acceptance-tests.md's closing paragraph states the opposite scope for the same table: "The Test Type column's classification markers on AC-002/AC-003/AC-004 (and every other AC) cite design.md's own Automated / Manual Classification Table (AC-025) directly... that table is this package's single normative classification source (REQ-007), fixed once and covering every check in this document" — and acceptance-tests.md's own rows for AC-025 through AC-030 each carry a Test Type value tagged "(classification: automated, design.md Classification Table)", i.e. sourced from that same table. A design.md author cannot determine, from this package alone, whether the Classification Table must enumerate 25 checks (REQ-001–REQ-005 lineage, per requirements.md's own explicit text) or all 30 (per acceptance-tests.md's explicit "covering every check in this document"); building the narrower table (as requirements.md instructs) would leave acceptance-tests.md's own claim that AC-025–AC-030's Test Type values are table-sourced unverifiable, and building the broader table would exceed AC-025's own stated scope. This is a direct textual contradiction between the two Phase-1 documents under review, not an implementation-time ambiguity, and it prevents an implementer from testably satisfying AC-025's own "exhaustive... never partial" criterion because "exhaustive over what set" is unresolved. Severity Critical: it is a contradiction between two frozen specification documents' own explicit scope statements for the same normative artifact, not a merely missing clarification.

The allowed input manifest for this review contains no domain/context-map.md or domain/domain-contract.json, and this check's file scope does not permit reading outside the five-file manifest to confirm or rule out a domain/ directory with an Approved model. Per calibration, when the Approved domain-model precondition cannot be established, this check is recorded as skipped.
